name: Snowball
description: Alone, then pairs, then all of us: one question distilled by everyone. Any question, any week.
when: When the class needs to agree on one thing and every voice should shape it.

solo: You can only add fractions when the pieces are the same size.
A fraction is a division problem that has not happened yet.
The bottom number says how many pieces, the top says how many you have.
Equivalent fractions are the same amount cut into different pieces.
Multiplying by a fraction less than one makes the number smaller.
Half of something small can be less than a quarter of something big.
Turning a fraction into a decimal is just doing the division.
One whole can be written a hundred different ways.

intro.message:
Three rounds: alone, together, all of us.

First you'll answer on your own, nobody can skip the thinking step. Then you and a partner will merge your answers into one; when their name appears on your screen, go sit next to them. Then the whole class sees what the pairs built.

solo.prompt: What is the most important idea from this unit?

pairs.instruction: Stand up and go sit next to your partner. Combine your answers into one stronger answer.

share.discussionPrompt: What changed when you combined your two ideas? Which line would not exist without the other person?

end.message: Started as everyone's own idea. Ended as a few strong ones, built by all of us.
